visual_goal: Show that the provenance envelope is filled in once at ingestion and travels with the fact into stores, derived facts, products and usage events, with batch and license fields stored by reference.
prompt: A left-to-right flow illustration. Far left: a cluster of generic source boxes (a small government building, a supplier server, a dealer laptop) under one label 'Sources'. One arrow from 'Sources' to a funnel-shaped intake box labeled 'Inlet', arrow labeled 'files and events'. From 'Inlet' one arrow right to a stack of three database cylinders labeled 'Fact stores', arrow labeled 'fact plus envelope'; each cylinder shows a small envelope icon attached to a data card. From 'Inlet' a second arrow down to a small filing-drawer box labeled 'Batch records', arrow labeled 'by reference'. Below-left of 'Batch records', a document-cabinet box labeled 'License register' with one arrow up into 'Batch records'. A thin dotted line links 'Batch records' to 'Fact stores'. From 'Fact stores' one arrow up-right to a gear box labeled 'Derived facts', and one arrow right to a screen box labeled 'Products'. One arrow from 'Derived facts' down into 'Products'. From 'Products' one arrow right to a receipt-roll box, arrow labeled 'fact versions served'. The receipt-roll box carries the label 'Usage events' exactly once, below it. Every label appears exactly once in the image.
alt: Sources feed Inlet, which writes each fact with its envelope to the fact stores and batch fields to batch records linked to the license register; fact stores feed derived facts and products, and products record the fact versions they served as usage events.

visual_goal: Show the life of one fact version: Active can become Superseded, Retracted or Disputed; Disputed returns to Active or becomes Superseded; nothing returns from Superseded or Retracted.
prompt: A simple state map of four rounded tiles on a light background. Left: a small black start dot with one arrow into a green tile 'Active', arrow labeled 'recorded'. Far right, on the same level as 'Active': a grey tile 'Superseded'. Top right, above 'Superseded': a grey tile 'Retracted'. Directly below 'Active': an orange tile 'Disputed'. Exactly five arrows between tiles: one straight horizontal arrow from 'Active' to 'Superseded' labeled 'correction'; one arrow from 'Active' diagonally up-right to 'Retracted' labeled 'wrong subject'; one arrow from 'Active' down to 'Disputed' labeled 'challenge'; one arrow from 'Disputed' up to 'Active' labeled 'rejected'; one arrow from 'Disputed' diagonally up-right to 'Superseded' labeled 'upheld'. 'Superseded' and 'Retracted' each have one short arrow out to the right into a small ringed end dot. No arrow points from 'Superseded' or 'Retracted' to any tile. Write every label as plain text without quotation marks.
alt: State map: a recorded fact version is Active; it can be superseded by a correction, retracted for a wrong subject, or disputed; a dispute is either rejected (back to Active) or upheld (Superseded); Superseded and Retracted are final.
